text:
support-liz: Hey team — customer (acct: ACME-889) says the daily usage chart is assigning events to the wrong day in the Console, and the CSV export doesn't match what the chart shows. They are in Europe/Paris. :confused:
samir: Can you paste the CSV example & a screenshot of the chart? Also which date range they selected?
support-liz: Screenshot attached in original thread (small). CSV row for 2026-03-14 has 18:45:12Z events but in the Console those same tokens are shown under 2026-03-13. They selected "last 7 days" and timezone in org settings is Europe/Paris.
elaine: Quick hypothesis: export pipeline uses event_timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' -> then truncates to day, but the UI applies org tz before truncating. Could be double-shift when DST is in play. Any DST change around that date?
robin-sre: Europe/Paris DST starts last Sunday in March — this date (Mar 14) is before DST. But I see code that uses to_char((created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date, ...) vs date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE org_tz. Might be inconsistent.
devops-bot: export-job-321 finished. job_id=321, tz_conversion=UTC->Europe/Paris, rows=402, runtime=23s
samir: Can you repro locally with acct timezone set to Europe/Paris + sample events at 22:45 UTC (23:45 CET) and 23:30 UTC (00:30 CET next day)? If UI truncates after converting to CET, and export truncates before converting, they'll land on different dates.
support-liz: I ran a quick check in Redshift: 
```
SELECT event_id, created_at, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS as_utc,
       (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Paris' AS as_paris,
       date_trunc('day', (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Paris') AS paris_day,
       date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS utc_day
FROM events
WHERE account_id = 'ACME-889'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 6;
```
Results show same raw timestamps but paris_day differs from utc_day for the late-hour events.
elaine: That SQL demonstrates the mismatch. Export pipeline currently uses utc_day (wrong) while UI uses paris_day. We should standardize to convert to org timezone before day truncation.
billing-ops: This is causing billing CSV rows to be attributed to the previous day for some customers. Any chance this affects invoicing cutoffs? Need quick patch.
samir: Quick mitigation: update CSV exporter to use the same helper as Console: helpers/date::day_in_tz(created_at, org_tz). I can open a hotfix PR to change the exporter job to call that helper.
robin-sre: Also add a unit test around DST edgecases and a small integration test that compares exporter vs UI day buckets across a sample window.
support-liz: Customer asked for a temporary workaround — can we tell them how to adjust their local CSV?
elaine: For now, advise them: if CSV date < expected by 1 day for events around 21:00-23:59 UTC, shift day by +1 when converting to Europe/Paris. We'll notify them when hotfix is deployed. :thumbsup:
samir: PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4321 — hotfix changes exporter to use day_in_tz. Marking high priority.
robin-sre: Deploying hotfix to staging now. tagging @billing-ops for a sanity check on invoices.
devops-bot: deploy job 987 started -> staging (hotfix/exporter-day-tz)
support-liz: Thanks team — I'll update the customer and add follow-up when staging validation complete. :pray:
